sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Elizabethtown, KY?
sections.html:
Owners in Elizabethtown can hire an agent, sell without one, or take an as-is cash offer, and the three routes differ mostly in time, repair spending and who handles the paperwork. Hardin County, not the city, bills the property tax and records the deed, so most of the practical steps run through county offices.

Elizabethtown is the Hardin County seat and the ninth-largest city in Kentucky by the 2020 count. It anchors a metro area that also takes in Meade and Larue counties, Radcliff, Vine Grove and the housing areas of Fort Knox. The right route depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need the money.

sections.h2: How big is the Elizabethtown housing market?
sections.html:
Elizabethtown grew faster than the other three Kentucky cities in this group: the Census Bureau counted 31,394 residents in 2020 and estimates 35,448 for July 1, 2025. Owners live in just under half of the homes here, so rentals make up a large part of the housing stock.

sections.h2: Where is Elizabethtown and why does location matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Elizabethtown sits in east-central Hardin County on Interstate 65, about 30 miles from Louisville and 80 miles from Bowling Green. The Western Kentucky Parkway starts at the I-65 interchange here, and the Bluegrass Parkway runs about 105 miles east to Lexington.

The town was surveyed in 1793 by Colonel Andrew Hynes and legally established in 1797, named for his wife Elizabeth. Thomas Lincoln lived in a log cabin here after his 1806 marriage, and Sarah Lincoln was born in the town in 1807. The Louisville and Nashville Railroad reached Elizabethtown on June 15, 1858, and the town became a trade center along the line.

The climate is humid subtropical, with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Before listing, have the cooling system serviced and check crawl spaces and basements for moisture.

Local jobs shape demand. Kruger Packaging announced a 400,000 square foot corrugated-box plant in the T.J. Patterson Industrial Park, with about 150 jobs planned, and a September 2026 announcement added a converting line that raises capacity by about 25%. Health care and social assistance receipts reached $880.7 million in 2022, the highest of the four cities.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Elizabethtown homes?
sections.html:
Two public districts serve the city, and the one a house belongs to can change how buyers see it. Elizabethtown Independent Schools runs Elizabethtown High School, T.K. Stone Middle School, Morningside Elementary, Helmwood Heights Elementary and Valley View Educational Center. Hardin County Schools covers part of the city limits, including Central Hardin High School and several elementary schools.

  • Some homes with an Elizabethtown mailing address sit in neighboring Radcliff and are zoned to schools there.
  • Central Hardin High School is inside Elizabethtown but uses a Cecilia mailing address.
  • Elizabethtown Community and Technical College is in town, and Western Kentucky University holds classes in a shared building.

Before you list, confirm the taxing district and school zone on your tax bill instead of assuming it from the address.

sections.h2: What does a seller pay at closing in Elizabethtown?
sections.html:
The seller pays Kentucky's real estate transfer tax, fifty cents for every $500 of value or fraction of it, and the county clerk collects it at the moment the deed goes on record (KRS 142.050). At the Census median home value of $245,900 that comes to roughly $246. Foreclosure transfers, transfers between spouses and nominal-price transfers between parent and child are among the exemptions the statute lists.

  • Payoff of the mortgage and any other recorded lien.
  • The seller's prorated share of the current year property tax.
  • Transfer tax, collected by the Hardin County Clerk at recording.
  • Agent compensation, if you list with one, which is set by your listing agreement.
  • Repairs or credits the buyer negotiates after inspection.

Call the Hardin County Clerk at 270-765-2171 for the payoff on any delinquent prior-year tax bill well ahead of closing.

sections.h2: How does Hardin County bill property tax on an Elizabethtown house?
sections.html:
The Hardin County Sheriff collects the bill, and the bill goes out in the name of whoever owned the property on January 1. The sheriff's office at 150 North Provident Way, Suite 101, takes payment by mail, in person or by card online, and the card fee is 2.49% of the total bill.

The published schedule for the bills issued each November runs like this:

  • November 1 through November 30: discount period.
  • December 1 through December 31: face amount.
  • January 1 through January 31: 5% penalty.
  • February 1 through April 15: 21% penalty.

Partial payments on a current-year bill are refused, and the sheriff will not accept a prorated payment from a seller and buyer separately. Whoever handles closing usually pays the full bill and settles the split on the statement. The sheriff's site lists separate city tax payment details only for tax districts 03 (Radcliff) and 06 (Vine Grove), so read the district number printed on your bill.

Homeowners 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can reduce the taxable value through the homestead exemption, which is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. The Hardin County PVA, at 270-765-2129, takes the application. The exemption belongs to the owner, so a buyer has to apply on their own.

sections.h2: What local rules affect selling a house in Elizabethtown?
sections.html:
The city's Code Enforcement Division handles property maintenance, zoning compliance, nuisance violations and unsafe conditions. An open complaint on an overgrown lot or a damaged structure can come up during a buyer's title and inspection review, so ask the division whether anything is on file for your address.

Permit history is a separate matter from code complaints. If you are unsure whether past remodeling was permitted, ask the city's Planning and Development department before you list.

Inherited houses add a step: the deed has to be put in the heirs' names or the estate's representative has to sign, so contact the county clerk and a Kentucky attorney early.

sections.h2: Which way of selling fits an Elizabethtown house?
sections.html:
Match the route to the house and your calendar.

  • Use an agent when the house shows well and you can wait on a buyer who needs a loan.
  • Go private when you already have a buyer and an attorney to draft the contract and deed.
  • Choose a cash offer when the house needs work, has tenants, owes back taxes or belongs to an estate.

Whichever route you pick, get the payoff figure, the tax bill and any code notices in hand before you compare offers.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax when I sell in Elizabethtown?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of value, paid by the seller. On a house valued at the Census median of $245,900, that is about $246. The Hardin County Clerk collects it at the moment the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: What are the Hardin County tax payment windows?
faqs.a: The discount period runs November 1 to November 30 and the face amount is due through December 31. A 5% penalty applies in January, and a 21% penalty applies from February 1 to April 15, when unpaid bills move to the clerk.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The seller and buyer split it by the days each owned the house, and the closing agent usually calculates the split. The sheriff will not take prorated payments, so one party pays the whole bill and the other settles up at closing.

faqs.q: Which office bills property tax on an Elizabethtown house?
faqs.a: The Hardin County Sheriff collects the bill. The sheriff's site points to separate city tax payment details for tax districts 03 and 06, which are Radcliff and Vine Grove. Read the district number on your own bill, and call 270-765-5133, option 1, if it is unclear.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Elizabethtown house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can purchase a house with open violations, but the city's Code Enforcement Division can tell you what is on file, and fixing or disclosing the problem avoids surprises at closing. Cash buyers commonly purchase houses in this condition.
